A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Pages 2–15 have identical text and rendered appearance; changes are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, and runtime measurements, including ImageNet-1k and CIFAR-100 results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–12 and the accompanying empirical analyses, including the supplementary learning curves and activation distributions.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same activation-statistics computation, global low-variance neuron selection, and mean-shift compensation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-classification coverage: ImageNet-1k in the main text and Appendix B, and CIFAR-100 in Appendix C. No dataset or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Magnitude and SNIP in Table 3, ToMe in Table 4, NViT in Table 5, and the pre-activation comparison in Table 7 are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same comparators.

E3.justification: Model configurations, pruning rates, metrics, optimizer settings, and ten-epoch fine-tuning remain identical. Appendix A retains the 100-epoch experiment, and Appendix D retains the same hardware timing comparisons.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the component ablations, pruning sensitivity analysis, and pre/post-activation comparison. Appendices A and E retain identical learning curves, layer-wise pruning analyses, and activation-distribution plots.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–12 and Figures 2–8 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same 80.67% final accuracy for DeiT-Base at 55% pruning in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains identical mathematical definitions, variance-based reconstruction-error reasoning, and the derivation that absorbs pruned neurons' mean contributions into the output bias.

C1.justification: The claims of efficient one-shot structured pruning, accuracy preservation with limited fine-tuning, architectural applicability, and compatibility with ToMe remain unchanged. The abstract retains the same quantitative headline results.

C2.justification: The explanations of pruning sensitivity, post-activation statistics, ToMe compatibility, and ConvNeXt accuracy retention are identical. No substantive applicability qualification or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and a GitHub link to boschresearch/variance-based-pruning at the end of the abstract; v1 provides neither. Other implementation and reproducibility details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning against earlier pruning approaches, and all 32 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract's background, removing the Vision Transformer example, resource-constrained-hardware emphasis, and hundreds-of-epochs phrase. It adds the code-access sentence and updates the arXiv stamp; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and placements are identical. The revised abstract and repository link fit within the existing abstract area without changing the page arrangement.

improvement.justification: The added repository pointer supplies previously missing code-access information, modestly improving implementation discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific arguments, experiments, and appendices are unchanged. The PDFs establish the documentation benefit but do not verify repository contents or executability.
